sentences.text:
Mohit Kumar @ Mohit Sharma vs State Of Uttarakhand on 20
February, 2023
Author: Ravindra Maithani

Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Second Bail Application No. 270 of 2022
Mohit Kumar @ Mohit Sharma ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the applicant.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant Mohit Kumar @ Mohit Sharma is in judicial custody in FIR/Case Crime No.0474 of 2021,
under Sections 363, 366A and 376 Ipc & Section 3/4 of Protection of Children From Sexual
Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Patel Nagar, District Dehradun.
He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

3. According to the FIR, on 16.09.2021, the applicant told it to the victim, a young girl of 13 years,
that her father had met with an accident.
He took the victim along with him in his room, laced her drink and raped her.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the victim has already been examined in the Court.
It is argued that the victim has admitted that her statement under Section 164 of the Code was given as told to her by the Police Officer.
It is argued that the allegations are false.
Applicant did not commit any wrong.
Hence, it is a case fit for bail.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the victim has supported the prosecution story when she was examined in the Court.
6. In her examination by Court, the victim has revealed her age at about 14 years.
She was born on 14.04.2008.
In her statement before the Court, she has supported the prosecution case as to what had happened to her.
The FIR was lodged on the same date.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In her statement given to the Investigating Officer, the mother of the victim reveals that on the date of incident at 01:00 in the noon, when the victim returned, she was not speaking to anyone and after some persuasion she could reveal as to what had happened to her.
8.
Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court is of the opinion that there is no ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the second bail application deserves to be rejected.
9. The second bail application is rejected.
10. Urgency Application (IA No. 4 of 2023) stands disposed of, accordingly.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 20.02.2023
